spec_match.rationale: Computes lag as event.timeStamp − result.audioEndTime per the explainer's latency-tracking use case, refuses to invent a number when timing is null, and correctly frames the threshold as informing an application-defined policy rather than providing a backend.

interactive.rationale: The threshold slider live-updates its readout and gauge marker (verified at 1500 ms/50%), the sample walkthrough animates four staged lag readings against the chosen threshold, and the live path runs a real continuous recognition.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises the timeStamp-minus-audioEndTime lag fed into an application-defined fallback policy, matching the page exactly.

edge_cases.rationale: Null/absent audioEndTime, no-SR browsers, recognition errors, threshold crossing both ways, sample-timer cleanup, and pagehide teardown are all handled without fabricated values.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus 5811907077472256 (verified) and the explainer's latency-tracking anchor are linked.

conformance.rationale: The all-manual suite (including the common-time-origin assertion this page relies on) honestly reflects that no automated check can run without a live timed result.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI: initial gauge, marker position, verdict, and transcript placeholder verified with clean console (fonts.googleapis.com failure environmental); the sample walkthrough and live path could not be clicked and there is no autorun hook.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts cover measured lag, null timing, no-SR, recognition errors, and sample runs, plus injected global error capture.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout, secondary/disabled button states styled with both background and color, and the rose failover verdict on stone (~4.9:1 bold) clears AA.

accessibility.rationale: The latency readout is aria-live, the verdict is role=status, the gauge's role=img label is updated with the actual ms values on every change, and the threshold slider is a labelled native range with focus-visible styling.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Harness-validated ok/ok recorded in responsive-support.json (2026-07-25); the gauge and controls are fluid and the code pre scrolls in place; this session's own 360px CLI capture is inconclusive due to the headless min-width clamp.

openQuestions.title: Add an autorun hook for the sample walkthrough
openQuestions.detail: Everything asserted about the moving gauge relies on clicking 'Play sample walkthrough'. A ?sample=1 query param that triggers the existing sample handler would let headless verifiers (and the conformance/critique loops) observe the gauge, over-threshold state, and verdict transitions without a pointer, at no cost to real visitors.

summary: A disciplined use-case demo: the lag arithmetic matches the explainer, null timing is surfaced instead of faked, the failover framing avoids overclaiming, and the gauge is one of the few visual meters in the corpus whose accessible label updates with its value. No defects found; the single open item is a testability hook. Verified with headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CLI (screenshots, DOM, clean console); interactive paths could not be driven in this environment, so runtime evidence is partial.
